newsitem.title: THAILAND: New Thai measures to pressure bank earnings.
newsitem.headline: New Thai measures to pressure bank earnings.

text.p: New Thai central bank measures to limit offshore loans by commercial banks will add pressure on local banks already hit by a sagging economy and slow loan growth, bankers said on Tuesday.
On Monday, the Bank of Thailand introduced measures to limit foreign loans granted through the Bangkok International Banking Facility (BIBF) branches of Thai and foreign banks in Thailand.
"There must be some impact on most banks' profit because the central bank basically does not want BIBF loans to expand," said Satian Tantanasarit, vice president at Thai Danu Bank.
The curb on BIBF loans granted by offshore banking units will also reduce the tax advantage of the BIBF facility over loans made through normal channels, he said.
"The impact on most banks' profit will not be significant as BIBF loans account for about seven to eight percent of banks' total assets," Satian said.

The slower earning growth of local commercial banks this year was attributed mainly to the sluggish demand for new loans as a result of the sagging economy, dull export trade and battered property markets.
"The earning growth for the overall (banking) industry will be at a single-digit level this year from more than 15 percent last year," said a senior banker at a local bank.
"It's very hard to expand credits under this economic circumstance," he added.
The Thai stock index has tumbled as foreign funds and investors sold off bank shares.
The SET index on Monday plummeted below the 1,000-point barrier to a 37-month low of 944.63.

Traders and analysts said persistent concern about most banks' slow earnings this year and about the adverse effect of new central bank measures to limit offshore loans provided the selling pressure on bank shares.
But bankers said the stock investors' worries about commercial banks' earnings this year was an overreaction because most banks' earnings will still grow this year.
